children.text: Magnetic field effects on superconductors

Electrons in a superconductor can lower their energy by Δ per electron by forming an opposite-spin, opposite-momentum Cooper pair. First model an electron as a uniformly charged ring with charge −e, mass m and radius r. Its angular velocity points along the ring normal n̂. The Bohr magneton is μB=eℏ/(2me)=\(5.788\times10^{-5}\) eV/T. In B write the common two-electron kinetic energy as K0=p1²/(2me)+p2²/(2me). Ignore orbital effects there. In C ignore spins and minimize the normalized real-wavefunction functional \[F=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\psi\left(-\alpha\psi-\frac{\hbar^2}{4m_e}\psi^{\prime\prime}+\frac{e^2B_z^2x^2}{m_e}\psi\right)dx,\qquad\alpha>0.\] In D, spin-orbit coupling gives opposite internal fields +Bz ẑ and −Bz ẑ to opposite-momentum electrons. These internal fields act on spin only. An external in-plane field Bx x̂ is perpendicular to them, and orbital effects of this in-plane field are ignored.

Find the magnitude and direction of angular momentum for angular speed ω.
a2. Orbital magnetic moment
Relate ring magnetic moment to its angular momentum.
a3. Orientation energy
If n̂ makes angle θ to a uniform field Bz ẑ, find U with U=0 at θ=π/2.
a4. Classical spin estimate
Use the ring gyromagnetic relation for spin projection ±ℏ/2. Find energies for spins parallel and antiparallel to B.
a5. Quantum spin energies
Quantum mechanics doubles the A4 values. Give both energies at B=1 T and use this convention subsequently.
b1. Pair energy
Find ES for a Cooper pair in a uniform field when only spin is affected.
b2. Normal-state minimum
Find the minimum energy EN of two unpaired electrons in an in-plane field Bx>0.
b3. Paramagnetic threshold
Find BP above which the normal state is preferred in this pair model.
c1. Optimal Gaussian
For \(\psi=(2\lambda/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-\lambda x^2}\), find λ minimizing F. You may use Gaussian normalization and ⟨x²⟩=1/(4λ).
c2. Orbital critical field
Find the critical |Bz| where the superconducting state is no longer energetically favoured.

a2. Orbital magnetic moment

a3. Orientation energy

children.text: Magnetic field effects on superconductors
a1. Ring angular momentum
The ring inertia is mr². Thus \(\mathbf L=mr^2\omega\hat{\mathbf n}\), with direction given by the right-hand rule.
a2. Orbital magnetic moment
The signed current is I=−eω/(2π), so \(\boldsymbol\mu=I\pi r^2\hat{\mathbf n}=-e\mathbf L/(2m)\). The magnetic moment is antiparallel to angular momentum.
a3. Orientation energy
Integrate magnetic torque or use \(U=-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B\). Thus \(U=er^2\omega B_z\cos\theta/2\). The positive sign follows because the ring charge is negative.
a4. Classical spin estimate
With the classical factor one, \(U_{up}=+\mu_BB/2\) and \(U_{down}=-\mu_BB/2\). These are estimates before the quantum spin factor is applied.
a5. Quantum spin energies
The corrected energies are U′up=+μBB=+\(5.788\times10^{-5}\) eV and U′down=−μBB=−\(5.788\times10^{-5}\) eV. Magnetic moment parallel to B means spin antiparallel to B.
b1. Pair energy
Opposite spin Zeeman energies cancel, so \(E_S=K_0-2\Delta\).
b2. Normal-state minimum
Both magnetic moments align with the field, lowering each electron energy by μBBx. Thus \(E_N=K_0-2\mu_BB_x\).
b3. Paramagnetic threshold
EN<ES when 2μBBx>2Δ. Thus \(B_P=\Delta/\mu_B\). This simplified two-electron criterion differs from the full condensation-energy Pauli limit by a factor √2.
c1. Optimal Gaussian

The expectation is \(F=-\alpha+\hbar^2\lambda/(4m_e)+e^2B_z^2/(4m_e\lambda)\). Set its derivative to zero with λ>0, obtaining \(\lambda=e|B_z|/\hbar\). The second derivative is positive. The field checks Bz>0.
c2. Orbital critical field
At the minimum \(F_{min}=-\alpha+e\hbar|B_z|/(2m_e)\). Setting it to zero gives \(B_c=2m_e\alpha/(e\hbar)=\alpha/\mu_B\).
d1. Ising pair energy
The two spins are opposite but each magnetic moment aligns with its own opposite internal field. Thus \(E_I=K_0-2\Delta-2\mu_BB_z\).
d2. Normal energy in crossed fields
The two total fields are (Bx,0,±Bz), both of magnitude \(\sqrt{B_x^2+B_z^2}\). Align each magnetic moment with its own total field, giving \(E_\parallel=K_0-2\mu_B\sqrt{B_x^2+B_z^2}\).
d3. Enhanced Ising threshold
At equality \(\sqrt{B_I^2+B_z^2}=B_z+\Delta/\mu_B\). Therefore \[B_I=\frac{\sqrt{\Delta^2+2\Delta\mu_BB_z}}{\mu_B}.\] It can greatly exceed BP when the internal spin-orbit field is large.
